name: LM5165XDRCR
title: Ultra-low-IQ synchronous buck converter, 150 mA, 3 V to 65 V in
summary: A synchronous step-down converter with both power MOSFETs inside (2 Ω PMOS high side, 1 Ω NMOS low side) that runs from 3 V to 65 V and delivers up to 150 mA. It draws 10.5 µA with no load. Grounding RT picks PFM for the best light-load efficiency; a resistor on RT picks constant on-time control at a near-fixed frequency; neither needs compensation. LM5165 is adjustable from a 1.223 V reference, LM5165X is fixed at 5 V and LM5165Y at 3.3 V. Four selectable peak current limits, internal or capacitor-set soft start, precision enable with adjustable UVLO hysteresis, open-drain power good, 100 % duty cycle and thermal shutdown come in a 3 mm × 3 mm VSON-10.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node: joined inside to the drains of the high-side PMOS and the low-side NMOS. The power inductor connects to it.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, feeding the high-side MOSFET and the internal bias LDO. Connect the input capacitor CIN with the shortest possible path.

pins.name: ILIM
pins.function: Current-limit select. A resistor to GND picks one of four peak current levels; shorted to GND gives the highest.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start set. Open: internal 900 µs ramp of the FB reference. 100 kΩ to GND: soft start off, the reference steps straight to full value at enable. A capacitor to GND sets a longer ramp.

pins.name: RT
pins.function: Mode select and COT on-time set. Shorted to GND: PFM operation. A resistor to GND: COT operation, the resistor setting the on-time and so the switching frequency.

pins.name: PGOOD
pins.function: Power-good, open drain. An internal NFET pulls it low while FB or VOUT sits below regulation. Needs a 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ pull-up to VOUT or another supply of at most 12 V.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Precision enable / UVLO comparator input; the converter turns on above 1.212 V.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output sense for the fixed 3.3 V and 5 V versions: joins the output to the internal feedback divider.

pins.name: HYS
pins.function: Open drain of an internal NFET, released when EN is above its threshold. A resistor from HYS into the EN divider sets the input UVLO hysteresis.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Regulator ground return.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad. Connect to GND and system ground; keep its path to CIN as short as possible.

circuits.title: Typical schematic, fixed 5 V output
circuits.description: An LM5165X takes 3 V to 65 V down to 5 V through a 68 µH inductor into 22 µF. EN is tied to VIN so the part runs whenever the supply is above its internal UVLO. RT and ILIM are grounded, giving PFM mode at the 240 mA peak current limit; SS is open for the internal 900 µs soft start, and PGOOD and HYS are unused. Below 5 V in, the output follows the input.

circuits.title: Design 1: wide-VIN, low-IQ COT converter, 5 V at 150 mA
circuits.description: A COT-mode LM5165X giving 5 V at up to 150 mA from 5 V to 65 V, with 12 V nominal. RRT = 133 kΩ from RT to GND sets the on-time for about 220 kHz to 230 kHz switching. CSS = 47 nF gives a 6 ms soft start. RESR, 1.5 Ω in series with the 22 µF output capacitor, adds ripple in phase with the switch node so the COT comparator sees enough of it at VOUT. ILIM is grounded for the 240 mA peak limit; EN is tied to VIN; PGOOD and HYS are left open. Target full-load efficiency is 91 % at 12 V in.
notes: Nominal switching frequency is stated both as 220 kHz and, for RRT = 133 kΩ, as 230 kHz.

circuits.title: Design 2: small PFM converter, 3.3 V at 50 mA
circuits.description: A minimum-part-count PFM converter: an LM5165Y makes 3.3 V at up to 50 mA from 3.5 V to 65 V, 12 V nominal. RT is grounded for PFM. RILIM = 56.2 kΩ selects the 120 mA peak current limit, and the 47 µH inductor then sets about 350 kHz pulse frequency at 12 V in. SS is open for the internal 900 µs soft start; EN is tied to VIN; PGOOD and HYS are left open. Target full-load efficiency is 88 % at 12 V in.

circuits.title: Design 3: high-density PFM converter, 12 V at 75 mA
circuits.description: An adjustable LM5165 in PFM mode making 12 V at up to 75 mA from 18 V to 65 V, 24 V nominal. RFB1 = 1 MΩ and RFB2 = 113 kΩ set the output against the 1.223 V reference. RUV1 = 10 MΩ, RUV2 = 825 kΩ and RHYS = 37.4 kΩ set the input UVLO to turn on at 16 V and off at 14.5 V. RILIM = 24.9 kΩ selects the 180 mA peak limit; with the 47 µH inductor the pulse frequency is about 500 kHz at 24 V in. CSS = 22 nF gives a 3 ms soft start. RT is grounded for PFM and PGOOD is unused. Full-load efficiency target is 92 % at 24 V in.

circuits.title: Design 4: high-efficiency COT converter, 3.3 V at 150 mA
circuits.description: A COT-mode LM5165Y giving 3.3 V at up to 150 mA from 3 V to 65 V, 24 V nominal. RRT = 121 kΩ sets roughly 160 kHz switching. A 0.5 Ω RESR in series with the 22 µF output capacitor supplies ripple for the COT comparator. CSS = 33 nF sets a 4 ms soft start. ILIM is grounded for the 240 mA peak limit; EN is tied to VIN; PGOOD and HYS are open. Below 3.3 V in, the output follows the input. Target full-load efficiency is 91 % at 24 V in.

circuits.title: Design 5: 600 kHz COT converter, 15 V at 150 mA
circuits.description: An adjustable LM5165 in COT mode making 15 V at up to 150 mA from 24 V to 48 V, 36 V nominal, riding through transients to 65 V. RRT = 143 kΩ sets about 600 kHz. RFB1 = 499 kΩ and RFB2 = 44.2 kΩ set the output; CFF = 10 pF across RFB1 raises the high-frequency gain from VOUT to FB to near unity, so the output ripple reaches FB directly. RUV1 = 10 MΩ, RUV2 = 681 kΩ and RHYS = 40.2 kΩ put the UVLO at 19 V on and 17 V off. CSS = 47 nF gives a 6 ms soft start. ILIM is grounded for the 240 mA limit; PGOOD is unused. Target full-load efficiency is 92 % at 36 V in.
notes: RESR is 0.5 Ω in the schematic and 2.2 Ω, 5 %, 0402 in the component list.

operation.text: A PMOS high-side switch and an NMOS synchronous rectifier are on the die. While the PMOS conducts, SW rises close to VIN and inductor current climbs at (VIN - VOUT)/LF; after it turns off and an adaptive dead time passes, the NMOS conducts and the current falls at -VOUT/LF. Duty cycle D is TON/TSW. The PMOS needs no bootstrap capacitor, and no loop compensation is needed in either mode.

Grounding RT selects PFM. The part then works as a hysteretic regulator in boundary conduction: it fires pulses that each ramp the inductor from zero to the selected peak current until FB passes the upper threshold (VREF2, 10 mV above VREF1), then sleeps with most circuits off while COUT carries the load; supply current approaches 10.5 µA during sleep. The sleep length depends on load and output capacitance. Wake-up from sleep to active takes 4 µs. Maximum output current in PFM is half the peak current: 25, 50, 75 or 100 mA for the 60, 120, 180 or 240 mA settings.

A resistor RRT from RT to GND selects constant on-time control. The on-time varies inversely with VIN, so the frequency in CCM stays nearly fixed; the loop regulates by varying the off-time. At light load the low-side switch turns off when inductor current reaches zero (diode emulation) and pulses are skipped, lowering the effective frequency; this happens once load current drops below half the peak-to-peak ripple. COT suits low-noise, higher-current, fast-transient designs; PFM gives higher light-load efficiency and lower quiescent current.

The PMOS can stay on continuously for low dropout. In COT mode a frequency foldback stretches the on-time when FB has not risen past the 4 mV dropout hysteresis, lowering the frequency until 100 % duty is reached as VIN falls toward VOUT. PFM passes to 100 % duty naturally.

LM5165X (5 V) and LM5165Y (3.3 V) have the feedback divider inside and sense the output on the VOUT pin. LM5165 senses through an external divider into FB, regulating FB at VREF1 = 1.223 V. RFB1 of 100 kΩ to 1 MΩ suits most designs: larger values draw less current, which matters for light-load efficiency, but above 1 MΩ the FB node picks up noise more easily.

The peak inductor current is limited cycle by cycle, sensed in the high-side MOSFET after a leading-edge blanking time; the comparator delay is 100 ns. ILIM to GND through 0 Ω, 24.9 kΩ, 56.2 kΩ or 100 kΩ sets 240, 180, 120 or 60 mA. In COT mode the ripple depends on VIN, VOUT and LF, so more output current is available than in PFM.

EN feeds a comparator with a 1.212 V reference and 68 mV hysteresis. It can be tied to VIN, driven by a logic signal, or fed from a divider RUV1/RUV2 to set an input UVLO level; a resistor RHYS from HYS into the divider adds hysteresis, since the HYS FET (80 Ω typical) releases once EN passes its threshold. Below about 0.6 V on EN the internal LDO is off and the part draws its shutdown current (4.6 µA at 12 V in). Between about 0.6 V and 1.212 V the LDO runs but switching stays off (standby). Switching begins when EN exceeds 1.212 V, provided the internal bias supply has cleared its own undervoltage level.

PGOOD is open drain and needs a pull-up of 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ to a supply of 12 V or less; a divider can bring a higher rail down. Its switch turns off when FB rises past 94 % of VREF1 and turns on when FB falls below 87 %. The rising edge has a 5 µs deglitch. It can sequence downstream converters by driving their EN pins.

Left open, SS gives an internal 900 µs ramp of the regulation reference. A capacitor from SS to GND, charged by 10 µA, sets a longer ramp, useful with large output capacitance or higher VOUT; a 100 kΩ resistor to GND disables soft start, and the output then charges at the current limit. CSS is discharged when the output is shut down by EN, UVLO or thermal shutdown. Since negative inductor current is blocked, the part starts monotonically into a prebiased output, waiting for the ramp to pass the existing voltage.
Switching stops when the junction exceeds 170 °C and restarts when it cools to 160 °C.

Lower frequency cuts switching and gate-charge losses and raises efficiency; higher frequency allows a smaller LC filter and a faster current slew for transients. At light load PFM sleeps longer and so draws less input current. The 180 ns minimum on-time limits the step-down ratio at a given frequency (Equations 9 and 10).

Pick LF for ripple of 30 % to 50 % of rated current at nominal VIN. Saturation current should sit well above the current-limit setting with margin for derating at temperature; ferrite cores saturate abruptly, raising ripple and losses. In PFM, add margin to IPK(PFM) for the 100 ns comparator delay: 10 % in Design 2, 50 % in the higher-frequency Design 3.

Use at least 1 µF of X5R or X7R ceramic at VIN, rated about twice the maximum input voltage because of DC bias loss, placed close to VIN and GND. Add bulk capacitance if the supply is more than about 5 cm away; a 4.7 µF electrolytic with about 0.5 Ω ESR damps input-filter resonance. The input capacitor carries an RMS current of about IOUT/2 in PFM; the output capacitor carries about IPK(PFM)/2.

In COT mode the FB comparator needs ripple in phase with SW. A resistor RESR in series with the output capacitor provides it (Equation 15). If the resulting output ripple is too large, a capacitor CFF across RFB1 brings the FB node close to unity gain from VOUT at high frequency, coupling output ripple directly onto FB.
The input supply must hold above 3 V while delivering the peak input current; its resistance should be low enough that an input current step does not drop VIN into a false UVLO trip.

The highest di/dt loop is CIN with the internal MOSFETs: keep CIN tight to VIN and GND with top-side ground returning to GND and the exposed pad. Keep the SW trace to the inductor short and only as wide as the current needs. Tie GND to the pad and to a heat-sinking ground plane, preferably with an inner ground plane for shielding, and use a via array under the pad to inner ground layers to keep TJ below 150 °C. Make VIN, VOUT and ground wide. Ground the FB, SS and EN parts to the plane at one point, away from switched and load currents. Put RFB1, RFB2 and CFF right at FB, which is high impedance; the sense line from the load may be long but should avoid SW, the inductor and VIN, ideally on another layer behind a ground plane, which matters most with divider resistors above 100 kΩ. Keep the RT and SS parts close to the device. The example layout is single-sided with an almost unbroken ground plane on the bottom.

LM5165 is the adjustable version, LM5165X fixed at 5 V and LM5165Y fixed at 3.3 V, all in the 3 mm × 3 mm VSON-10 with 0.5 mm pitch; the LM5165 and LM5165X also come in VSSOP-10. It is pin-compatible with the LM5166. An automotive LM5165-Q1 exists. The family meets EN55022 / CISPR 22 EMI limits, with active slew-rate control of the switch node.
